lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 15: DaemonSets, Jobs and CronJobs
lesson.description: Run one Pod per node with a DaemonSet, run work to completion with Jobs, retries and parallelism, and schedule it with CronJobs, all tested on kind.
lesson.tested: Every command ran on a three-node kind v0.33.0 cluster (node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2) on 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: A DaemonSet keeps one Pod on each matching node. A Job runs Pods until enough succeed or retries run out. A CronJob creates Jobs on a schedule.

cheatsheet.intro: One Pod per node, work that finishes, and the commands from Lesson 15.

rows.name: DaemonSet
rows.role: One Pod on every qualifying node. There is no replicas field. DESIRED is that node count.

rows.name: Job
rows.role: Runs Pods until enough succeed, or retries run out. Failed Pods stay when restartPolicy is Never.

rows.name: Indexed Job
rows.role: Each Pod gets an index from 0. The hostname is the Job name plus the index.

rows.name: CronJob
rows.role: Creates a Job on a five-field schedule. Set timeZone or the controller manager's zone is used.

rows.name: completions
rows.role: How many Pods must succeed. The batch Job set this to 6.

rows.name: parallelism
rows.role: How many Pods may run at once. The batch Job set this to 2.

rows.name: backoffLimit
rows.role: Retries before the Job is Failed. Delay starts at 10s and doubles, capped at ten minutes.

rows.name: restartPolicy
rows.role: Never or OnFailure. Never keeps each failed Pod so you can read its logs.

rows.name: TTL
rows.role: ttlSecondsAfterFinished deletes the finished Job and its Pods. Stable since v1.23.

rows.name: History
rows.role: The report CronJob kept 2 successful Jobs and 1 failed Job.

rows.name: Overlap
rows.role: Forbid skips a tick while a Job is still running. Replace stops the old one. Allow overlaps.

homework.intro: Use the three-node kind cluster from part 3 and the namespace k8s-from-zero. The lesson's cluster is k8s-ep13, with one control plane and two workers. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What sets the number of Pods in a DaemonSet, and why was DESIRED 2 on the three-node cluster?
exercises.a: There is no replicas field. DESIRED is the number of nodes that qualify. The control plane is tainted node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule, so the agent stayed off it until the template tolerated that taint.

exercises.q: What do completions, parallelism and Indexed mode each do?
exercises.a: completions is how many Pods must succeed (default 1). parallelism is how many may run at once (default 1). Indexed mode gives each Pod an index from 0 in JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX, and the hostname is the Job name plus that index.

exercises.q: What does timeZone change, and what does concurrencyPolicy Forbid do?
exercises.a: timeZone is an IANA name such as Etc/UTC. Without it, the schedule follows the kube-controller-manager's zone. Forbid does not start a new Job while one from this CronJob is still running. The default policy is Allow.

exercises.q: Apply the node-agent DaemonSet and run kubectl get daemonset node-agent. What does DESIRED mean here?
exercises.a: In the lab it was 2: the two workers. The control plane did not qualify until the toleration was patched in, and DESIRED then became 3.

exercises.q: Wait for job/batch with --for=condition=complete. What did the lesson record for completions, duration and indexes?
exercises.a: Complete, 6/6, 18 seconds. completedIndexes was 0-5 and succeeded was 6. The logs were item 0 through item 5, each on a Pod named batch-N.

exercises.q: Run kubectl create job report-now --from=cronjob/report. What is that command for?
exercises.a: It creates a Job from the CronJob template immediately, so you can test the template without waiting for the schedule.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: A DaemonSet shows fewer Pods than you have nodes. What does the lesson tell you to check?
exercises.a: Look at DESIRED and at the missing node's taints with kubectl describe node. Add a toleration only for nodes the agent should run on, or fix the node selector.

exercises.q: A Job is Failed with reason BackoffLimitExceeded, and restartPolicy is Never. Can you still read the logs, and will this Job try again?
exercises.a: The failed Pods stay, so kubectl logs on each one still works. The retries are spent. Fix the command and create the Job again. A failed Job does not restart.

exercises.q: A CronJob fires at the wrong hour, or stops creating Jobs after the controller was down. What does the lesson name?
exercises.a: A missing timeZone follows the controller manager's zone. More than 100 missed schedules makes the controller give up with too many missed start times. Set startingDeadlineSeconds. Overlapping runs are the default Allow; use Forbid or Replace when runs must not overlap.
